question: Which set of LVEF cut-offs correctly classifies the three major heart failure phenotypes?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. An LVEF of 35% would still be classified as HFmrEF in older literature but the current threshold for HFrEF is ≤40%, not <35%.
Correct. Current ESC/ACC-AHA criteria: HFrEF ≤40%, HFmrEF (mildly reduced) 41–49%, and HFpEF ≥50%. These distinctions drive different management pathways.
Incorrect. The boundary values matter: HFrEF is ≤40% (inclusive), HFmrEF is 41–49%, and HFpEF is ≥50% (inclusive). An LVEF of exactly 40% is HFrEF, not HFmrEF.
Incorrect. These figures do not match any guideline definition. The accepted thresholds are HFrEF ≤40%, HFmrEF 41–49%, HFpEF ≥50%.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the LVEF classification table: HFrEF ≤40%, HFmrEF 41–49%, HFpEF ≥50%. Boundary values are commonly tested.
Well done. Precise LVEF thresholds are essential — an LVEF of exactly 40% is HFrEF, and ≥50% is HFpEF.
